source.title: You can graft SDF changes from base models onto post-trained models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses synthetic-document fine-tuning to install model behaviors and evaluates grafting as a way to reduce SDF-related damage. It does not measure whether insecure-code fine-tuning causes misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts.
record.gate_note: The post names the emergent-misalignment insecure-code corpus as an application of grafting, but gives no result for its unrelated-prompt misalignment behavior. It also says grafting maintains behavioral expression without reporting a corresponding measure here. The reported reality-drift, preference, capability, and tool-use results concern related but different outcomes; they are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The post evaluates grafting SDF updates to reduce coherence and capability damage. It only mentions applying grafting to the emergent-misalignment insecure-code corpus, with no reported rate of misaligned free-form answers. No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude grafting is a cheap swap-in for native SDF that avoids much coherence and capability damage. They also say it works for the insecure-code EM corpus, but the post reports no misalignment numbers for it.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates synthetic-document fine-tuning and grafted weight updates, not the original claim's matched insecure-code and benign fine-tuning comparison measuring neutral-prompt misalignment.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says graft benefits depend on training the graft from the base checkpoint; grafting from an instruct stage to later RL does not work as well. It also reports weaker reality-drift recovery in its weak-post-training experiment than with the off-the-shelf post-trained Qwen model.

fits_no_version.finding: Native SDF narrows the real-versus-made-up reality gap and lowers μ-decisiveness. Grafting from base partly restores both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grafting base-model SDF updates onto post-trained models reduces SDF-induced reality drift and preference-coherence damage.

fits_no_version.finding: Native SDF harms GPQA, XML tool calling and GSM8K. Grafting recovers much of this loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grafting mitigates SDF capability and tool-use costs.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-reviewed status not stated
record.problems: The post provides no uncertainty estimates. Several results are summarized without absolute scores, including the false-facts comparisons; the model for those results is not identified in the text. The post also notes that its mid-training experiment used weak post-training on a small model.
record.rows_left_out: No additional quantified results from the text were left out. Qualitative claims about grafting on the emergent-misalignment insecure-code corpus and maintaining behavioral expression are not accompanied here by a reported outcome measure for the claim's target behavior.

untested.parts: No misaligned-answer rate on unrelated questions after insecure-code training, and no secure or educational controls. The insecure-code corpus is mentioned only as a grafting application.
No other narrow datasets with a broad-misalignment outcome.
The authors state they did not measure misalignment via RL.
Neither inoculation nor benign re-training is tested. Grafting is not shown to affect emergent misalignment.
No effect size, seed robustness, coherence filtering, or training-stage onset for misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: The emergent-misalignment link is a single sentence in the conclusion: grafting "also works" for the insecure-code corpus. The post gives no outcome for it, possibly because it is in the full paper (arXiv:2610.00767). Rows r11–r14 do not name the model.

versions.untested_parts: No rate of misaligned free-form answers on neutral questions for insecure-code training or matched controls.
No broad-misalignment outcome for the listed alternative narrow datasets.
No test of broad misalignment arising from reinforcement learning.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature.
Grafting is evaluated as a way to reduce SDF damage, not the specified inoculation framing or brief benign retraining mitigation for broad misalignment.
The post does not report the size, seed robustness, coherence-filter robustness, or training-stage onset of the claimed broad misalignment.
